added_failures_note: The reviewed run's manifest records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm (both null), so the added-failure pair is derived from my own measurements at the reviewed base and head over the same target set (tests/discovery tests/core tests/llm tests/graph/test_path_prefix_filter.py): base 6d3d51576 2467 passed / 0 failed, head 4f91ac6c4 2468 passed / 0 failed, both EXIT=0. The head arm adds one passing test (test_ingest_claim_refuses_name_stage_relevance) and no failing id, so added_failure_count reads 0 with no ids.

findings.text: follow-on: the score stage now emits "skipped": r.path not in decided_paths in its per-file progress payload, so a file whose content decision failed is reported to the progress layer as skipped even though the same commit deliberately defers it for retry rather than dropping it. progress.py:475 renders a score row with skipped=True as a terminal "skip" (score_terminal="skip"), so an operator watching the run sees a deferred file as a finished skip. TRIGGERING INPUT: a file whose content decision fails (asyncio.gather return_exceptions=True drops it from content_decisions) -- apply_file_scores writes nothing and the file is reclaimed on the next score pass, yet its on_progress entry carries skipped=True. The plan states scoring does not skip a file; the deferred file is retried, not skipped. Counters are unaffected (run_skipped is incremented only from triage results at progress.py:749), so the impact is the per-row rendering only. The base revision emitted "skipped": False unconditionally, so the field's new meaning is introduced by cb8092d0a.

follow-on: when every file in a batch is deferred (no content decision succeeded), scored_count is 0, so score_cost_per_file and content_cost_per_file are 0.0 and the batch's description-call cost (batch_cost) is written to no CodeFile -- apply_file_scores guards the write with `if scored_items:` and returns deferred=len(matched) with an empty scored_items. TRIGGERING INPUT: a batch of N files whose N content decisions all fail. The spend is not lost from the run (score_worker still adds `cost` and `content_cost` to state.score_stats.cost, and the retry re-issues the description call and attributes it then), so this is a per-file attribution gap that self-corrects, not a leak. It is new only in that the prior apply_file_scores always wrote a scored item and so always distributed the batch cost.

item_verdicts.diff: three commits over the previously reviewed head 6d3d51576 - cb8092d0a (gate code ingestion on the content-arm decision), af1a5d81d (cover the content-stage ingest gate and the retry path) and 4f91ac6c4 (refresh the evidence fragment and figure) - 225 insertions and 187 deletions across 7 files.

item_verdicts.manifest: the reviewed run's manifest reads status complete with six commits and names gate.log, focused.log and negative_control.log; it records no baseline_suite and no after_suite arm, so the added-failure pair is derived from my own base and head arms over the same target set.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the gained three-commit diff touches exactly the declared write paths (imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py, parallel.py, scorer.py, workers.py, tests/discovery/test_code_relevance.py, the evidence fragment and the figure) and nothing outside them.

justifications.durability: The fix makes the fail-closed guarantee real rather than nominal: the content-stage requirement is applied at the claim, the has-work predicate and both stats counts so a run never counts, awaits or admits a name-only file; the retry path is correct because claim_files_for_scoring writes only claimed_at/claim_token and never status, so a deferred file stays status='triaged' is_enriched=true and is reclaimable, while release_file_score_claims clears its claim; and the now-redundant apply_content_decisions is deleted with no dangling re-export (imas_codex/discovery/code/__init__.py never imported it). One deduction: a batch whose every content decision fails attributes its description-call cost to no file, a self-correcting attribution gap noted as a nit.
justifications.evidence: The head arm is reproduced exactly (2468 passed, EXIT=0) and the base arm measured at the previously reviewed head (2467 passed, EXIT=0), both over tests/discovery tests/core tests/llm tests/graph/test_path_prefix_filter.py with the venv shadowed by PYTHONPATH; the delta is exactly the one new passing test, so added_failure_count is 0. The declared negative control is reproduced independently: removing the ingest claim's `AND sf.relevance_stage = 'content'` filter in a scratch copy of the head tree reddens exactly test_ingest_claim_refuses_name_stage_relevance (1 failed, 7 passed, EXIT=1), so the guarded comparison fires and the ingest stub's stage predicate is derived from the query text rather than hard-coded. One deduction: the reviewed run's own manifest carries no baseline_suite/after_suite, so the added-failure pair is my own measurement rather than one the run recorded.
justifications.fit: The added symbols are mechanism-named (relevance_stage, decided_paths, deferred), the rewritten comments state the implemented mechanism rather than the guarantee the old text claimed, and the docs fragment and figure are refreshed to match the code. Three deductions, all small and naming/semantic: the score stage's progress payload reuses the triage field name `skipped` to mean 'deferred for retry', which progress.py renders as a terminal skip; the `deferred` count returned by apply_file_scores is the only place that distinction is named; and no test asserts the on_progress skipped value, so the misleading meaning is unpinned.
justifications.goal_fidelity: The gained commits implement the plan's fail-closed clause and close the three findings of the prior review of this run. The ingest claim (workers.py:650-653), has_pending_code_work (graph_ops.py:740-744) and both pending counts in get_code_discovery_stats (parallel.py:449-453, 494-497) now require relevance_stage='content', so a name-arm relevance can never carry a file into ingestion; a failed content decision writes nothing (apply_file_scores builds an item only for a file with a decision) and leaves the file at its prior status with its claim released, so the next score pass reclaims and retries it. The prior review's dead triage_description read-back (graph_ops.py) is removed, the false score_worker comment is rewritten to the implemented mechanism, and the sibling-group key is restored to pid = row["parent_id"]. One deduction: the score stage's progress payload now sets skipped=True for a deferred file, which reads as a skip although the plan says scoring does not skip and the file is in fact retried.
justifications.reuse: Strong. apply_file_scores is widened to carry both the description scores and the content-arm relevance in one write rather than adding a third write path; _relevance_item and _relevance_set_clause build the relevance fields once; CODE_RELEVANCE_EXPR remains the single definition every gate interpolates; and the content-arm decisions call is reused from the decisions-call node through acall_decisions. The redundant apply_content_decisions is removed, and the previously residual triage_description read is deleted, so no reader of a retired field remains.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the three-commit gained diff lies inside the node's declared write paths and nothing outside them was touched; the commits are conventional with bodies, carry no AI attribution, and name no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in the message, the symbols or the comments.
